title: Born in East Malvern
summary: Born on the kitchen table at 13 Coppin Street, East Malvern, to journalist and Victoria Cross recipient William Dunstan and his wife Marjorie.

title: Family moves to Toorak
summary: Aged four, moves with his family to 20 Wallace Avenue, Toorak, the home he would describe as a cosy womb and leave only reluctantly for boarding school a decade later.

title: Enters Wadhurst, Melbourne Grammar's prep school
summary: Aged seven, begins at Wadhurst, the preparatory school of Melbourne Grammar, an Anglican school founded in 1849. A left-hander, he is beaten into writing right-handed by his form teacher Miss Baker.

title: Moves to Melbourne Grammar senior school
summary: Transfers from Wadhurst into the senior school; consistently near the bottom of the class in mathematics, placed on a daily report card system by headmaster Mr Caffin, and caned regularly.

title: Black Friday bushfires at Lorne
summary: Victoria's worst bushfire disaster burns through Airey's Inlet toward Lorne while the family is staying at Erskine House. The family shelters on the beach; his father drives through flames at high speed to reach them.

title: Begins boarding at Geelong Grammar School
summary: Begins four years as a boarder in Francis Brown House at Geelong Grammar, Corio. Assigned number 62 in a house hierarchy of 68 boys. Discovers Beethoven, studies under Manning Clark, and learns to endure cold showers at 6.30 a.m.

title: Australia enters the Second World War
summary: Aged 14, listens to Prime Minister Menzies announce war and immediately begins a scrapbook of clippings tracking the conflict, with a particular focus on Royal Air Force aircraft and Battle of Britain kill tallies.

title: First flight in an aeroplane
summary: Takes his first flight as a cadet in the Air Training Corps, from a flying field near Geelong Grammar, and joins Bob Dalziel in the ATC to secure priority in the RAAF call-up.

title: Sits Matriculation examinations
summary: Passes Matric in four mathematics subjects, physics and chemistry, after science teacher Charles Cameron provides private tuition from 5 a.m. Cameron's verdict: 'You have no brains at all. But you do have guts.'

title: Enlists in the Royal Australian Air Force
summary: Joins the RAAF with school friend Bob Dalziel on his 18th birthday. Posted to No. 2 Initial Training School, Bradfield Park, Sydney, where they are immediately patronised as rookies by the trainees who arrived three days earlier.

title: Pilot training begins at Benalla
summary: Transferred by his father via Air Commodore F. R. W. Scherger to No. 11 Elementary Flying Training School, Benalla, to train as a pilot on Tiger Moths rather than as a wireless air gunner.

title: Goes solo for the first time
summary: Flies solo at Benalla after nine hours and ten minutes of instruction under Flight Sergeant Bill Dale. One of the happiest moments of his life: 'I'M FREE! I'M FREE! I'M GOING SOLO.'

title: Advanced training at Deniliquin
summary: Posted to No. 7 Senior Flying Training School, Deniliquin, to fly Wirraways; chooses single-engine training, hoping to be a fighter pilot rather than a bomber crew.

title: Posted to Morotai
summary: Posted to No. 9 Transport and Movement Office on the Indonesian island of Morotai, a staging point for strikes into Borneo. Works round the clock as shipping officer unloading Liberty ships. The island is the base for Mustang squadrons of 81 Wing.

title: Lands at Labuan with the assault force
summary: Participates in the amphibious assault on Labuan, Borneo, aboard United States LSTs. Serves as RAAF representative with the Australian Beach Group, Ninth Division. Reaches the rank of Flight Lieutenant.

title: Discharged from the Royal Australian Air Force
summary: Discharged at No. 1 Personnel Depot at the Melbourne Cricket Ground after three years of service as Flight Lieutenant. Issued with an austerity Victory suit; his father promptly arranges a handmade replacement from family tailor J. Dunstan Lewis.

title: Joins the Herald and Weekly Times as a cadet journalist
summary: Against his father's advice, approaches Archer Thomas, editor of The Herald, and is hired without telling anyone. His father discovers three days later, but never again calls him a potential hack. Cadet training is four years, rotating between the Herald and the Sun News-Pictorial.

title: Marries Marie Rose McFadyen
summary: Marries Marie Rose McFadyen, niece of his mother's closest friend Doris McFadyen, whom he had first contacted during the war by posing as an identity card inspector to reach her at Presbyterian Ladies' College.

title: Foreign Correspondent, New York
summary: Appointed US correspondent for the Herald and Weekly Times. The honeymoon is the posting: a flight across the Pacific in a Boeing Stratocruiser. Sets up home at Forest Hills, Long Island, from where he covers the United Nations, interviews Frank Sinatra, and meets a 'shy, diffident' young Rupert Murdoch.

title: First child born in New York
summary: First child born at Cornell Hospital, New York, in one of the earliest public experiments in natural childbirth.

title: Foreign Correspondent, London
summary: Moves from New York to London as the Herald and Weekly Times's British correspondent; the family lives in Wallington, Surrey. Covers the death of Sir Keith Murdoch in October 1952.

title: Returns to Australia
summary: Sails home from London aboard the P&O liner Strathmore with Marie and two children. Arrives to find that the Herald and Weekly Times has taken up the option to buy the Courier-Mail and editor Colin Bednall has resigned.

title: Joins the Courier-Mail, Brisbane: 'Day by Day' column
summary: Begins writing a daily column, 'Day by Day', for The Courier-Mail in Brisbane; the family lives in Queensland for approximately four years before returning to Melbourne.

title: 'A Place in the Sun' column begins in the Sun News-Pictorial
summary: Returns to Melbourne and begins a daily column in The Sun News-Pictorial, Melbourne's largest-circulation newspaper. The column runs for twenty years and establishes him as a Melbourne institution.

title: Begins writing for The Bulletin as 'Batman'
summary: Takes on a regular column in the Sydney-based national weekly magazine The Bulletin under the pseudonym 'Batman', after Melbourne's controversial founder John Batman.

title: Founding secretary of the Anti-Football League
summary: Establishes a tongue-in-cheek organisation that pokes fun at Melbourne's Australian rules football obsession, and which attracts a large and loyal membership among those who agree that the city's fixation has gone too far.

title: First president of the Bicycle Institute of Victoria
summary: Becomes founding president of what is now Bicycle Network, serving until 1978. An enthusiastic commuter and long-distance touring cyclist, he later cycles across the United States and through China with his wife Marie.

title: President of the Melbourne Press Club
summary: Elected president of the Melbourne Press Club for 1976 and 1977, succeeding Rohan Rivett.

title: 'A Place in the Sun' column ends after twenty years
summary: Concludes two decades of the daily 'A Place in the Sun' column in The Sun News-Pictorial.

title: US West Coast Correspondent for the Herald and Weekly Times
summary: Appointed United States West Coast Correspondent for the Herald and Weekly Times, based in California. During the posting he and Marie tour the country by bicycle, later the subject of the book 'It's All Up Hill' with cartoonist Jeff Hook.

title: Returns from US posting; begins writing for The Age
summary: Concludes the US West Coast posting and returns to Melbourne, where he becomes a regular columnist and occasional contributor to The Age.

title: Cycles through China with Marie
summary: Tours China by bicycle with his wife Marie in the mid-1980s.

title: Crowned King of Moomba
summary: Crowned King of Moomba, Melbourne's largest free community festival, held each year along the Yarra.

title: Awarded the Medal of the Order of Australia (OAM)
summary: Recognised in the January New Year Honours for service as a journalist and author, and to the community, particularly as a supporter of the Berry Street Babies Home.

title: Patron of the Prahran Mechanics' Institute
summary: Appointed Patron of the Prahran Mechanics' Institute.

title: Died in Melbourne
summary: Died of cancer in Melbourne, aged 88. His son David reported that Keith had written his own self-effacing obituary. He had already been told of his forthcoming posthumous induction into the Victorian Media Hall of Fame.

title: Inducted into the Victorian Media Hall of Fame
summary: Posthumously inducted into the Melbourne Press Club's Victorian Media Hall of Fame, one month after his death.
